hooks.command: jq -c '(.tool_input.max_tokens // 4096 | tonumber? // 4096) as $n | if $n > 1500 then {hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", updatedInput: (.tool_input + {max_tokens: 1500})}} else empty end' || true

jq -c '.tool_response | strings | capture("exceeds maximum allowed tokens. Output has been saved to (?

[^[:space:]]+)") | (.p | rtrimstr(".")) as $p | {hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: ("The result above was saved to " + $p + " because it exceeded the inline output limit; the call itself succeeded. Read all of it before your next step. JSON is often a single line that Read offset/limit cannot chunk: probe its structure with jq (type, length, keys), then extract every record with jq; slice plain text with python. State how much you read, for example 87/87 records, before relying on it.")}}' || true
